source.title: Evaluation Awareness Scales Predictably in Open-Weights Large Language Models
source.authors: Maheep Chaudhary; Ian Su; N. Hooda; N. Shankar; Julia Tan; Kevin Zhu; Ashwinee Panda; Ryan Lagasse; Vasu Sharma

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how evaluation-awareness probe scores vary with model size and setup. It does not test held-out pretraining loss, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or downstream task performance, and does not rely on the specified loss-scaling findings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports an analogous scaling result for evaluation-awareness probe AUROC, a different construct from the loss and downstream-performance outcomes in the claim versions. Those results are recorded under fits_no_version, not as tests of V1–V7. Its AUROC values are presented in figures rather than tabulated.
record.test_reason: The study measures linear-probe AUROC for evaluation awareness across instruction-tuned models of different sizes. It reports no held-out pretraining loss, no compute or token sweeps, no compute-optimal allocation, no architecture-shape effects on loss, and no downstream task performance. It uses 'scaling law' only as a framing for a different construct and does not cite or rely on the original sources. None of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that evaluation awareness, measured by linear-probe AUROC, follows a power-law increase with model size that holds across families and enables forecasting in larger models. The plotted fit is labelled square-root. The record should also note that this conclusion rests on 10 models after excluding Qwen, whose results contradict the trend.
record.recipe_differences: Uses contrastive activation probes and AUROC on evaluation-context prompts, rather than measuring held-out language-modeling loss over parameter, token, or compute sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: For GPT-OSS-20B, the Hugging Face default chat template produced substantially higher AUROC peaks than the mock Harmony and Jinja2 templates. Qwen models did not follow the reported increase with model size.

fits_no_version.finding: In 10 non-Qwen instruction-tuned models (0.27B–70B), best-layer probe AUROC distance from 0.5 rises with parameter count. The trend is fit as y = a√x + b and described as a power law. No exponent or uncertainty is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear-probe signals of evaluation awareness strengthen with model size in open-weights instruction-tuned LLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Qwen-2.5-Instruct models (0.5B–32B) do not show the size trend and were excluded from the main analysis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The size trend in evaluation-awareness probe scores is not consistent across model families.

fits_no_version.finding: For GPT-OSS-20B, peak probe AUROC is substantially higher with the default Hugging Face chat template than with mock Harmony or Jinja2 templates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured evaluation awareness depends on the prompt template.

record.peer_reviewed: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025)
record.problems: The paper does not provide tabulated AUROC values, fitted exponents, or quantified uncertainty for the plotted trends. Its results concern probe-based evaluation awareness rather than loss scaling. The authors note limitations in generalizing across Mixture-of-Experts and proprietary frontier models.
record.rows_left_out: Layer-wise probe-score curves and Qwen layer-depth patterns (Figures 2 and 5) are not separately recorded; they describe probe location rather than the loss-scaling versions or the principal related size-scaling finding.

untested.parts: Pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute: not measured.
Extrapolating loss fits from small to large runs: not done.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation: not studied.
Effects of architecture shape on loss: not studied.
Loss power laws in other modalities or training regimes: not studied.
Downstream task performance versus scale or loss: not measured. Probe AUROC for evaluation awareness is not a downstream task score.
Dependence of loss-law exponents and allocations on fitting choices: not studied.

record.verdict_notes: Off-topic for loss scaling: it borrows the 'scaling law' label for a probe-AUROC trend. Small sample: 10 models in the main fit, with 1–5 per family, and only one GPT-OSS size. There are no error bars, no fitted exponent, and post hoc exclusion of the family that did not fit. The record's T6 and no-labels outcome is correct.

Whether loss power laws fitted on small runs predict loss on much larger runs.
The loss-minimising allocation of parameters and tokens for fixed compute, and its scaling with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details on held-out loss at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream task performance as a function of model scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of loss-scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices.

rows.operation_detail: Measured the best-performing linear probe's AUROC absolute distance from 0.5 across model sizes.

conditions.value: Situational Awareness Dataset (SAD), Stages Oversight subset
Four model families; aggregate scaling trend

rows.value: Figure only; the text describes a clear upward power-law trend with model size.
rows.note: The paper reports a trend across models, not a tabulated aggregate value or fitted exponent. This is evaluation-awareness probe performance, not held-out loss.
rows.check: Subject count is wrong. Excluding Qwen, the main analysis covers 10 models: Gemma-3 (5), Phi-3 (2), Llama-3.1 (2) and GPT-OSS-20B (1). The '15 models' total includes the 5 excluded Qwen models. Figure 1's legend calls the fit a square-root fit (y = a√x + b), which the text calls a power law. The construct is probe AUROC, not loss.
